# Tŷ Mawr — The Great House Farm Story — llms.txt

> The true story of the Williams/Buckler family and Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, Wales, in 99 scenes across 8 acts with a prologue and epilogue, in strict date order.
> Every scene is drawn from the Great House Farm Wiki evidence catalogue (https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/) and carries its evidence links.
> Structured JSON (acts, cast, scenes, evidence, stable ids): https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/api/timeline.json
> Printable script (static HTML, no JavaScript needed): https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/story/
> Storyboard: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?view=storyboard · Cast: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?view=cast · Any scene: https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/?event=<id>

## About

The Williams family lived at Great House Farm, beside St Dochdwy's Church, Llandough, for generations (by the family's account since 1667). The family's case is that the farm was two parcels: the house parcel (Parcel A), which passed out of the Bute estate to Daniel Thomas in 1877 and became the family's freehold when quarrying ended in 1928, and the eastern fields (Parcel B), which went to Western Ground Rents in 1938 and to BP. The possession cases of 1955, 1962, 1974 and BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 decided possession; none of them examined the documents that bear on the family's title to the house parcel. BP demolished the farmhouse on 6 December 1988, the morning after Cadw declined to list it, before it could be fully recorded. In 1994 an early-medieval cemetery of 1,026 burials was excavated on the site. Since 2025 the family have been recovering the missing records, and Cadw, Heneb and HM Land Registry's Independent Complaints Reviewer are now investigating. The family's case is that fraud and concealment kept the title documents from the courts, so the case can be reopened.

Truth labels follow the Wiki: documented fact, family evidence, reconstruction, legal inference and unresolved. The 1978–79 Llandough Roman Villa is a separate site south of the church.

## Full Timeline

99 scenes, in strict date order.

### P.1 (1). c. AD 650 — The church beside the house

Prologue: The Great House · Scene id: ghf-06500101-1 · Date: 0650-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

Long before there is a farm, there is a church. St Dochdwy's at Llandough is one of the oldest Christian sites in Wales, the seat of an early monastery. Beside it, on the slope above the river, stands the place that will become Tŷ Mawr: the Great House.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### P.2 (2). 12th – 14th century — An old house

Prologue: The Great House · Scene id: ghf-12000101-1 · Date: 1200-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Archaeological record

In the Middle Ages people live and work on this slope; their pottery is still in the ground eight hundred years later. The house that grows here is old, and it is grand: a long stone house the Royal Commission will judge sub-medieval, probably of the seventeenth century, perhaps built around something older still.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### P.3 (3). 1552 – 1829 — Cydfin, or Tŷ Mawr

Prologue: The Great House · Scene id: ghf-15520101-1 · Date: 1552-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Estate papers

In the manor's leases it goes by an older name: Cydfin, or Tŷ Mawr, a farm of a hundred and seven acres. For nearly three centuries the leases are kept, signed and filed.

- Estate papers: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records D 219: Llandough manorial leases and agreements, 1552–1829 — https://archives.library.wales/index.php/llandough-manorial-leases-and-agreements
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### P.4 (4). Mid 16th – late 18th century — The Vaughans of Great House

Prologue: The Great House · Scene id: ghf-15600101-1 · Date: 1560-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Heritage record

Great House is the chief freehold farm of the parish. For two hundred years the Vaughans, a minor gentry family, hold it. Their memorials are still in the church next door.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### P.5 (5). 1667 — The Williamses arrive

Prologue: The Great House · Scene id: ghf-16670101-1 · Date: 1667-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

In 1667 the Williams family come to Great House. Mary Williams, born there two and a half centuries later, will say her ancestors bought it. From now on, for more than three hundred years, there is a Williams in the house.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — origins — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### P.6 (6). Early 19th century — The Marquesses of Bute

Prologue: The Great House · Scene id: ghf-18000101-1 · Date: 1800-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Heritage record

Early in the nineteenth century the Bute Estate, the greatest landowner in South Wales, takes the freehold. The manor courts of Llandough and Leckwith sit in the house itself. By 1818 Llandough's rents are in Bute's books, and in 1824 the estate's surveyor walks the farm and writes it down.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Wiki page: The Bute Estate — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bute-estate/
- Estate papers: National Library of Wales, Bute Estate Records R1: Glamorgan Estate rentals — https://archives.library.wales/index.php/glamorgan-estate-rentals
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations (Stewart survey, D/d B E/1–2) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### P.7 (7). c. 1840 — The Great House shrinks

Prologue: The Great House · Scene id: ghf-18400101-1 · Date: 1840-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Public record

Then, on paper, the Great House begins to shrink. In the census and the tithe returns it stops being 'Great House' and becomes 'Great House Farm': no longer the court house of a manor, just a farmhouse. It is the first time the records make the place smaller than it is. It will not be the last.

- Wiki page: Farmhouse Nomenclature — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/farmhouse-nomenclature/
- Wiki page: Name & Location Variations — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/great-house-farm/name-variations/

### I.1 (8). c. 1858 — Bones by the church

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18580101-1 · Date: 1858-01-01 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Museum record

Workmen digging foundations beside the church find six skeletons, a medieval spearhead and a spur. The bones are put back in the ground by the churchyard stile. Llandough's dead lie close under the surface. Nobody yet asks how many there are.

- Museum record: 1931 letter, Museum Wales file 63.24 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/ghf-e106-r33-a1-1931-letter-museum-wales-file-63-24/
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### I.2 (9). c. 1870 — The soldier under the floor

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18700101-1 · Date: 1870-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Under the dining-room floor of the Great House, the family will always say, lies a soldier in armour, with his horse, his lance and a small shield. The story is told for a hundred years. It reaches the Daily Telegraph and the Royal Commission's files. Nobody ever lifts the floor to look.

- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974 (dates the find to "about 1870") — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### I.3 (10). 1876 – c. 1912 — The quarrymen

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18760101-1 · Date: 1876-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Estate papers

Limestone brings the quarrymen. The Bute Estate lets about thirty-three acres of the farm to the Llandough Limeworks, and for the next thirty-five years the quarry eats into the land.

- Wiki page: Llandough Limeworks — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/llandough-limeworks/

### I.4 (11). 1877 — The farm is cut in two

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18770101-1 · Date: 1877-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Mary's statement

In 1877 the estate divides the farm. It sells the farmhouse, its buildings and about ten acres to the quarryman Daniel Thomas, and keeps nine acres of fields on the top. The Williamses stay on as tenants of both, and, as Mary will tell it, with a promise: when the quarrying ends, the house comes to them. From this year Great House is two parcels with two owners. Everything that follows turns on that line, and on the paper that drew it. That paper is now missing.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — the sale — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#sale-1877
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — plan — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#plan
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — Bute lease — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#sale-1877

### I.5 (12). 11 November 1891 — Three geese

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18911111-1 · Date: 1891-11-11 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Newspaper

Fourteen years later three geese are stolen from "Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough". The thief goes to court, and the newspaper records, in passing, who lives at the house.

- Newspaper: 1891 court report — farmyard theft — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n01

### I.6 (13). May 1897 — Marconi

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-18970501-1 · Date: 1897-05-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

In May 1897 Marconi sends the first wireless signals across open sea, from Lavernock Point to Flat Holm. In the family's memory it is Thomas Williams of Great House who carts his equipment down to the point.

- Newspaper: Press report of the Lavernock trials, 1897 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n02

### I.7 (14). 1908 — John Williams takes over

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-19080101-1 · Date: 1908-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Mary's statement

Mary's grandfather dies, and her father, John Williams, takes over: the house under the Thomases, the fields under Bute. Two parcels, two landlords, one family.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: John Williams — 1908 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/john-williams/#y1908
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (1905 Bute conveyance) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### I.8 (15). 10 August 1913 — Mary is born

Act I: The Bargain · Scene id: ghf-19130810-1 · Date: 1913-08-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

On 10 August 1913 Mary Williams is born in the farmhouse. She will live in it for the rest of her life, and she will die in it.

- Wiki page: Mary Williams — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/
- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/

### II.1 (16). February 1916 — "The whole farm"

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19160201-1 · Date: 1916-02-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Court record

In 1916 Bute lets John Williams "the whole farm" on a yearly tenancy. Bute no longer owns the house; it sold it in 1877. But those two words, "whole farm", will be read for the next seventy years as if it did. The tenancy itself does not survive. Only the words do, quoted in a judgment seventy years later.

- Court record: The 1916 Tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1916-tenancy/#grant
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Farm / Whole Farm Nomenclature — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/whole-farm-nomenclature/

### II.2 (17). 1928 — The last rent

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19280101-1 · Date: 1928-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

In 1928 the last of the quarry machinery leaves. John Williams pays a final rent of about four pounds to Alfred Thomas, and the bargain of 1877 comes due. From now on the house is the family's own. Mary sees the receipt. It will not survive.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — takes effect 1928 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#takes-effect
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (15 May 1924 agreement) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### II.3 (18). 1936 — Mary marries Frederick

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19360101-1 · Date: 1936-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Mary marries Frederick Buckler, a farmer, and he comes to live with her in the house. They will have seven children; the first, a son, is born within a few years.

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — marriage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#marriage
- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### II.4 (19). 1938 — Sold to Western Ground Rents

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19380101-1 · Date: 1938-01-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

In 1938 Bute sells out to a property company, Western Ground Rents. It sells what it still has at Llandough: the fields, and its interest as landlord. It cannot sell the house. It no longer owns it.

- Wiki page: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#y1938
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### II.5 (20). May 1939 — The plan

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19390501-1 · Date: 1939-05-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Document

A year later Western Ground Rents gives John Williams a new tenancy, with a plan. The plan shows the fields east of the house. The house is not on it.

- Wiki page: 1938–39: the 1939 tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#y1939
- Wiki page: The 1939 tenancy plan — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#plan

### II.6 (21). c. 1940 — Twelve years

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19400101-1 · Date: 1940-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family case

By 1940 John Williams has lived in the house for twelve years without paying anyone a penny for it. In law, twelve years is enough. If the bargain of 1877 had not already made the house his, time has.

- Wiki page: 1938–39 — c. 1940 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1939-revised-tenancy/#c1940

### II.7 (22). 1944 — War on the land

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19440101-1 · Date: 1944-01-01 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Mary's statement

The war is on, the farm is struggling, and the War Agricultural Committee wants it run better. Frederick takes over the fields as manager for his father-in-law.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: John Williams — 1944 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/john-williams/#y1944

### II.8 (23). c. 1948 – 49 — Billy is born

Act II: The House Is Theirs · Scene id: ghf-19480101-1 · Date: 1948-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

William Buckler, Billy, is born at the farm. He will be the last of the family to live there, and the one they evict.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### III.1 (24). 2 February 1949 — Nothing in writing

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19490202-1 · Date: 1949-02-02 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

In February 1949 John Williams gives up his tenancy of the fields, and Frederick takes them on from Western Ground Rents. Nothing is written down. Mary, whose house it is, is not part of it. But from now on the landlord will talk of Frederick's tenancy as a tenancy of "the farm", house and all.

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — the 1949 tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/

### III.2 (25). June 1950 – c. 1952 — The blanket box

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19500601-1 · Date: 1950-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

In 1950 an estate agent from Penarth places a lodger in the farmhouse. He stays two years. Before he goes, he tells Mary what he has done: he has taken the papers from the family's blanket box, 'including the agreement relating to the farm', and handed them to the agent. The family's proof of title leaves the house in a lodger's hands. It is never seen again.

- Mary's statement: Mary Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — papers taken — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#papers-taken

### III.3 (26). 1952 – 53 — The last rent on the fields

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19521010-1 · Date: 1952-10-10 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

In October 1952 the landlord's agents write that they will not go on letting the fields to Frederick. He pays his last rent the next year. After that the family pay no one.

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — 1952 letter — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### III.4 (27). 2 February 1955 — The first order

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19550202-1 · Date: 1955-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Court record

In February 1955 the High Court orders Frederick to give up possession of "the whole farm". Mary, who owns the house, is not in the case and is never heard. On 4 July the landlord comes to take it all. Mary has just come home from hospital. She stands her ground, and they take the fields and leave the house.

- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#order
- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — enforcement — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#enforcement

### III.5 (28). 1959 — Mary says no

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19590101-1 · Date: 1959-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

In 1959 Western Ground Rents offers Mary a tenancy of her own farmhouse and garden. She refuses. The house is hers, she tells them, and there are documents to prove it. The documents are already gone.

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — 1959 refusal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#refusal-1959
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### III.6 (29). 11 December 1962 — The second order

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19621211-1 · Date: 1962-12-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 11 December 1962, in Cardiff County Court, Judge Temple Morris QC orders Frederick and Mary out of the farmhouse and garden, and makes them pay for every year back to 1955. The order is made. It is never carried out. Mary stays.

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#order
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (29 March 1961 deed) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration

### III.7 (30). June 1963 — Committal

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19630601-1 · Date: 1963-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The landlord goes after Frederick for the money, and committal proceedings follow. The threat of prison now hangs over the family for staying in their own home.

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — committal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#committal
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### III.8 (31). January – March 1965 — Two pounds a week

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19650301-1 · Date: 1965-03-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Document

In March 1965 the agents try again: a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden for 'Mrs Williams', at two pounds a week. Mary does not sign it, does not send it back, and does not pay. From now on even the landlord counts her as living there in her own right, not theirs.

- Wiki page: The 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#offer-1965
- Wiki page: Mary Williams — 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#chronology

### III.9 (32). 1964 – 68 — A rumoured sale

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19640101-1 · Date: 1965-06-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Family account

Somewhere in these years, a cousin will later say, the eldest son sells "our land parcel" through a solicitor, behind his parents' backs. No document has ever come to light. In 1968 he and his household leave the farm.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — rumoured sale — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### III.10 (33). 1967 — Frederick dies

Act III: The Papers Vanish · Scene id: ghf-19670101-1 · Date: 1967-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

Frederick Buckler dies at fifty-six. Mary takes back her maiden name, Williams, and stays on in the house she was born in.

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#death

### IV.1 (34). 31 December 1969 — BP buys in

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19691231-1 · Date: 1969-12-31 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

On the last day of 1969 Western Ground Rents sells Great House Farm to the BP Pension Trust, the pension fund of British Petroleum. That conveyance will become the root of BP's title. Today it cannot be found in the Land Registry's files.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### IV.2 (35). 1970 – 72 — Plans drawn around her

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19720725-1 · Date: 1972-07-25 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Around Mary the plans are already being drawn. In 1970 land by Leckwith Road is registered as a village green. In July 1972 planning permission is granted for houses on the site, with Mary still living in the middle of it.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### IV.3 (36). 1974 — Half a survey

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19740101-1 · Date: 1974-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

The Royal Commission sends a surveyor to record the old house. He gets as far as the ground floor. The rest, he notes, cannot be examined 'because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute'. The house will never be fully recorded.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### IV.4 (37). 15 April 1974 — Open day

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19740415-1 · Date: 1974-04-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 15 April 1974 Mary, now sixty, opens her home to the public 'to show what the nation is losing'. Hundreds come, and a thousand sign a petition. The Daily Telegraph reports that BP's pension fund has permission for thirteen houses, that Mary will not move, and that her solicitors say she has a valid claim to the house.

- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, 'Open day to save ancient Welsh house' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Wiki page: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action

### IV.5 (38). 3 July 1974 — Mary pleads ownership

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19740703-1 · Date: 1974-07-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

BP Pension Trust sues for possession. In her defence Mary pleads, plainly, that the house is hers, and the Limitation Act besides. The case is part heard and adjourned. It is never brought back. Her claim to own the house is never tried.

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the action — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### IV.6 (39). September – October 1974 — The licence letters

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19741031-1 · Date: 1974-10-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

In September BP gets leave to enforce the old 1962 order; Mary is given no notice. Then, on 31 October, BP withdraws the warrant and writes to her instead, 'licensing' her to live in the house rent-free for life. Mary never asked for a licence, and never accepts one. She does not believe BP owns her house. But BP keeps the letters.

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#letters
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the warrant — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#warrant

### IV.7 (40). 19 November, 1970s (year unclear) — "Grievous loss"

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19741119-1 · Date: 1974-11-19 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

A letter to the Western Mail warns that pulling down Great House would wipe out the site of St Dochdwy's Celtic monastery, and traces the land back through Tewkesbury Abbey to the Crown. The letter is printed. Nothing changes.

- Newspaper: Western Mail, 'Grievous loss' (letter) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n04
- Wiki page: The Restoration Campaign — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/restoration-campaign/#open-day-1974

### IV.8 (41). 1975 – 1980 — "The most rapacious ground landlord"

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19800522-1 · Date: 1980-05-22 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Parliament

In 1975 the pension fund passes its interest to BP Properties. In May 1980 Ted Rowlands MP tells the House of Commons that Western Ground Rents, 'the most rapacious ground landlord' in South Wales, has been bought by the BP pension fund. The landlord that first came for the farm in 1955 now belongs to BP.

- Newspaper: Hansard, 22 May 1980 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n16
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### IV.9 (42). 1 October 1982 — A warning about the ground

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19821001-1 · Date: 1982-10-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In October 1982 GGAT, the regional archaeological trust, warns the planners that the ancient settlement may run north of the church, under the farm, and asks for thorough investigation before anything is built.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Newspaper: Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980 (Roman villa, a separate site) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n05
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 18 March 1983 — burnt relics (Roman villa finds, a separate site) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n06

### IV.10 (43). 19 – 30 November 1982 — First registration

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19821119-1 · Date: 1982-11-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

In November 1982 BP's solicitors apply to register the land at HM Land Registry for the first time. Mary is seventy and living in the farmhouse. Nothing on the file shows anyone asking her what she claims.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1982–83 Registration & Opportunity to Object — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1982-83-registration-opportunity-to-object/

### IV.11 (44). 23 February 1983 — The farmhouse title

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19830223-1 · Date: 1983-02-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

In February 1983 they apply again, for the farmhouse and garden on their own: a separate title, WA240304. The application certifies that BP knows of no question or doubt about its title. The woman who told a court nine years earlier that the house is hers is living in it.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### IV.12 (45). 26 March 1983 — Mary dies

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19830326-1 · Date: 1983-03-26 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

On 26 March 1983, a month later, Mary Williams dies in the farmhouse where she was born. Her son Billy inherits her claim, and her fight.

- Wiki page: Mary Williams — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#death
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### IV.13 (46). 8 April – 12 May 1983 — Letters after her death

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19830408-1 · Date: 1983-04-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

Two weeks after Mary's death, BP's solicitors and the Land Registry are writing to each other about the farmhouse file. Whatever the Registry asked about the family in the house, and whatever it was told, is in those letters.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.1 (47). 1984 — BP's writ

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19840522-1 · Date: 1984-05-22 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

In January 1984 the register is reissued. In May BP Properties issues its writ for possession of the house. Its case rests on the licence letters of 1974, the letters Mary refused. That same year, the family learn, the library's copy of the 1877 deed between Bute and Daniel Thomas goes missing.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — the writ — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#writ
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — library copy missing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#library-1984
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.2 (48). 10 July 1986 — Judgment for BP

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19860710-1 · Date: 1986-07-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 10 July 1986, in the High Court at Cardiff, Mr Justice Hollis finds for BP. The 1974 letters, he holds, gave Mary a licence, so she was never in possession against BP. The deed of 1877, the receipt of 1928 and the plan of 1939 are not before him. The question of who owns the house is never put.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — High Court — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#high-court
- Analysis: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/court-judicial-issues/bp-v-buckler-scope-decided-undecided/

### V.3 (49). 1986 – 87 — A file goes missing

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19860711-1 · Date: 1986-07-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

While the case goes on, the Royal Commission's correspondence with Mrs Buckler goes missing from its files: letters in which she may have told an independent public body, in her own words, why the house was hers.

- Analysis: Legal Review — the loss pattern — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#loss-pattern

### V.4 (50). 2 February 1987 — Two titles become one

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19870202-1 · Date: 1987-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 2 February 1987, with the appeal still to be heard, the Land Registry is asked to fold the farmhouse title into BP's main title. The separate record of the family's house disappears into the whole.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — amalgamation — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1987-hmlr-amalgamation-during-appeal/

### V.5 (51). 31 July 1987 — The Court of Appeal

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19870731-1 · Date: 1987-07-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 31 July 1987 three judges in the Court of Appeal dismiss Billy's appeal. The 1962 action, they hold, stopped the clock, and BP's letters made Mary's possession permissive whether she accepted them or not. The documents she spoke of are not produced. Nor is the newspaper that reported her claiming the house in 1974. BP Properties Ltd v Buckler goes into the law books as a leading case on adverse possession. The family's story does not.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Analysis: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — what it omits — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#omits

### V.6 (52). 3 March 1988 — Twenty-eight days

Act V: Possession, Not Ownership · Scene id: ghf-19880303-1 · Date: 1988-03-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 3 March 1988 the House of Lords refuses leave to appeal. The family are given twenty-eight days to leave a house the Williamses have lived in for three hundred years.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — House of Lords — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#house-of-lords

### VI.1 (53). 29 April 1988, morning — The bailiffs come

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880429-1 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

29 April 1988. Five bailiffs and fifteen police officers come up the lane. Billy blocks the narrow drive with a tractor, locks the doors and bars the windows.

- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on', c. 30 April 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 29 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-01) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.2 (54). 29 April 1988 — The chainsaw

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880429-2 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The bailiffs smash the gate and take poleaxes to the doors. When an axe comes through a door with his three small children behind it, Billy starts a chainsaw and pushes it through. The bailiffs fall back. After four hours they leave. Branwen takes the children away. BP tells the press it let Mary stay out of kindness. Billy tells them the farm is theirs.

- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 April 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-02) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.3 (55). May 1988 — "Someone will be killed"

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880512-1 · Date: 1988-05-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Billy takes his case to the European Commission of Human Rights in Strasbourg. On 12 May the Cardiff MP Alun Michael asks the Lord Chancellor to look at it again. Billy warns that someone is going to be killed.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 12 May 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-03) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr

### VI.4 (56). 29 July 1988 — Cadw comes to look

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19880729-1 · Date: 1988-07-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Photograph

On 29 July Cadw, the Welsh heritage body, comes to look at the house for listing, and photographs the farmhouse and the barn. Those two photographs are all that is left of the visit. No notes, no file, no record of who decided.

- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the barn, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/

### VI.5 (57). 29 – 30 November 1988 — Forced entry

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881130-1 · Date: 1988-11-30 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

29 November. The bailiffs come back, and this time they force their way in. Within hours, the family say, the demolition has begun: half the roof is already off an outbuilding. Billy is taken to Llandough Hospital. Eight other people living at the farm lose their homes with the family.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo front page — 'Angry scenes as farmer evicted' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n14
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 30 November 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-04) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'Billy's unhappy family' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n09

### VI.6 (58). 1 December 1988 — Everything in the road

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881201-1 · Date: 1988-12-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Billy lies injured in hospital. Branwen and the children have nowhere to go. Mary's whole life, her photographs, the family heirlooms, the legal papers, is left in the house or thrown into the road. Billy has the clothes he stands in.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 13 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-11) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.7 (59). 2 December 1988 — Do not touch the house

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881202-1 · Date: 1988-12-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 2 December a High Court judge orders that the farmhouse and everything in it must not be touched. Branwen may go in for her belongings, if BP's solicitors agree. BP says it means to demolish and build new homes on the ten acres.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — 'History fight to save farm' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 2 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-05) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VI.8 (60). 3 December 1988 — From hospital bed to the dock

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881209-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Police take Billy from his hospital bed and charge him with assaulting two bailiffs, criminal damage, and furious driving.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-06) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n15

### VI.9 (61). 3 – 5 December 1988 — One weekend

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881203-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Over one weekend, without setting foot inside, Cadw considers emergency listing. In public it says it is looking at the house. In July it had already marked it just below the bar.

- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — Cadw considering spot-listing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08

### VI.10 (62). Monday 5 December 1988 — Nothing more we can do

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881205-1 · Date: 1988-12-05 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Monday 5 December. Judge Norman Francis refuses to keep the injunction in place until Strasbourg can hear the family. Their solicitor says there is nothing more they can do. The same day Cadw announces that the house is not of sufficient merit to list. Nothing now protects it.

- Newspaper: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — 'Farmer fails in final eviction hearing' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n10

### VI.11 (63). 6 December 1988, 4am — Bulldozed before breakfast

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881206-1 · Date: 1988-12-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

6 December 1988. Just after four in the morning, a twenty-strong team arrives with bulldozers. By breakfast no building is left standing. Branwen and the children watch their home go. Three centuries of the Williams family, the old court house of the manor, the soldier under the floor: gone before the day has begun.

- Newspaper: 'Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n11
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-07) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 21 December 1988 (reader's letter on "Bulldozed Before Breakfast") (search extract GHF-E090-N15-12) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VI.12 (64). 7 – 9 December 1988 — Like a battlefield

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881208-1 · Date: 1988-12-07 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Llandough is furious. A county councillor, himself a BP pensioner, calls it 'disgusting'. Villagers confront their councillors. The council's planning chief, the family remember, says the site looks like a battlefield. On 9 December magistrates bail Billy on condition that he stays away from the land he was born on.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 7 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-08) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 9 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-09) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 10 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-10) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Wiki page: 1988: Possession and Demolition — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/demolition-1988/

### VI.13 (65). December 1988 — In the rubble

Act VI: Bulldozed Before Breakfast · Scene id: ghf-19881212-1 · Date: 1988-12-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

In the rubble a Royal Commission investigator finds what the bulldozers left: a carved fireplace jamb, and a moulded beam of a kind rare in Glamorgan. And he records what is lost: a carved stone capital that stood by the front door, probably taken long ago from the old church.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VII.1 (66). 20 March 1989 — Clearing the site

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890320-1 · Date: 1989-03-20 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 20 March 1989, at half past seven in the morning, the lorries move in to carry away what is left.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 20 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-14) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.2 (67). January – March 1989 — "I will fight on"

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890323-1 · Date: 1989-03-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

In January one charge is dropped as out of time, and Billy is told not to come within half a mile of the site. On 23 March he pleads guilty to the rest and walks free. He will fight on, he says, for his home and for more than seventy acres of land.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 23 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-15) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 24 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-16) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: 'Charge against evicted farmer dropped', January 1989 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n12
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 January 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-13) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.3 (68). 1989 — From farm to a bus

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890325-1 · Date: 1989-03-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The family who lived in the Great House now live with Billy's sister in Penarth. Billy plans to make a home in an old bus. Thirty thousand pounds' worth of his belongings, he says, were taken from the site after the demolition.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 1989 — 'From farm to a bus' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n13

### VII.4 (69). 14 April 1989 — Strasbourg says no

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19890414-1 · Date: 1989-04-14 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

In April 1989 Strasbourg rules. The European Commission accepts that the eviction interfered with Billy's home, but finds it lawful, and closes the case.

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr
- Court record: Buckler v United Kingdom, Commission decision (PDF) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/wp-1790112811838.pdf

### VII.5 (70). October – November 1989 — BP applies to build

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19891107-1 · Date: 1989-11-07 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In November 1989 BP applies for permission to build houses on the farm. GGAT advises that nothing should be decided without an archaeological assessment. Then BP hires GGAT to do it. Their report calls the lost farmhouse 'a county treasure'.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings

### VII.6 (71). February – March 1990 — "Unfortunately demolished"

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19900313-1 · Date: 1990-03-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In March 1990 outline permission is granted. The planning officer notes that the Local Plan said the farm buildings should be kept, 'however they were unfortunately demolished a little while ago'. No preservation notice was ever served. Part of the archaeologists' advice is missing from the file.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.7 (72). August – October 1990 — Eight trenches

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19900801-1 · Date: 1990-08-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In August 1990 GGAT cuts eight trenches for BP. They find early medieval burials. A large area they could not investigate is marked as low potential, and in October the council signs the archaeology off.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.8 (73). 21 August 1991 — The obituary

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19910821-1 · Date: 1991-08-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

In 1991 the official heritage record writes the house's obituary. It 'was suddenly and completely demolished by B.P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy'.

- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VII.9 (74). 14 May 1992 — Twenty houses

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920514-1 · Date: 1992-05-14 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

In May 1992 Ideal Homes applies to build twenty detached houses on the farm.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.10 (75). 15 May 1992 — Billy dies

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920515-1 · Date: 1992-05-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family account

The next day, 15 May 1992, Billy Buckler dies of a heart attack in Llandough Hospital, in the village where he was born. He is buried at Michaelston-le-Pit. He never gets his home back.

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### VII.11 (76). 27 July 1992 — A warning, half missing

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920727-1 · Date: 1992-07-27 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Planning file

In July 1992 GGAT warns the council that the ground holds significant remains, medieval and perhaps older, and human bone. Page two of the letter is missing from the file.

- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.12 (77). 3 September 1992 — Approved anyway

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19920903-1 · Date: 1992-09-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

Thirty-eight days later the twenty houses are approved, with no new archaeological condition.

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.13 (78). December 1993 — The diggers move in

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19931203-1 · Date: 1993-12-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

In December 1993 BP transfers the land to Ideal Homes, and the diggers move in before the archaeology has been dealt with. GGAT asks the council to stop the work. The developer produces a barrister's opinion that the condition is met. The council accepts it: 'a difference of opinion', it later tells the MP.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.14 (79). March – July 1994 — A thousand graves

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19940504-1 · Date: 1994-03-21 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In the spring of 1994 the excavators find what the trenches missed. Burial after burial lies just below the topsoil, in the ground the 1990 report called low potential. By the end there are more than a thousand: the largest early medieval burial ground ever found in Wales. For at least two weeks of the dig, the Home Office licence to remove the dead has run out. The work goes on.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.15 (80). 28 July 1994 — Who owns the dead

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19940728-1 · Date: 1994-07-28 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Museum record

In July 1994 Ideal Homes, as owner of the land, gives the human remains and finds to the National Museum of Wales. The dead of St Dochdwy's pass from a developer to the state.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.16 (81). 1994 – 96 — Church View Close

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-19941110-1 · Date: 1994-11-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

In November 1994 the woodland above the house, part of the family's parcel, passes to the Forest of Cardiff. The power lines go in. The houses go up. Church View Close is built over the farm.

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.17 (82). 2005 — The cemetery in print

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-20050101-1 · Date: 2005-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In 2005 the cemetery is published in a learned journal: 1,026 burials. It tells the story of the dead. It does not tell the story of the family whose home stood over them, or of how that home came down.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Publication: Holbrook and Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/

### VII.18 (83). 20 March 2019 — Nearly thirty years late

Act VII: Built Over · Scene id: ghf-20190320-1 · Date: 2019-03-20 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Heritage record

In 2019 GGAT's 1990 report on Great House Farm is finally added to the national record, nearly thirty years after it was written, and thirty years after the house was gone.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

### VIII.1 (84). November 2025 – January 2026 — The grandchildren

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20251117-1 · Date: 2025-11-17 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Official correspondence

In November 2025 Mary's grandchildren start asking for the records. The community council says it cannot help. Cadw's email addresses bounce, the first of many. In January 2026 they ask the Land Registry to put back on the record the claim that was left off it in 1983.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.2 (85). February – March 2026 — "No evidence of a mistake"

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260323-1 · Date: 2026-03-23 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Land Registry retrieves its old paper files. In March it replies: there is 'no evidence of a mistake in the register'. It treats the farm as one holding. It does not say how the house got into BP's title.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026
- Official correspondence: HMLR holding letter, 13 February 2026 (PDF) — https://github.com/unclehowell/datro/blob/wayback/wayback/pdf/foi/2026-02-13_hmlr_wa231076_holding-letter.pdf

### VIII.3 (86). 19 April – 25 May 2026 — "Registered correctly"

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260419-1 · Date: 2026-04-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The family complain of fraud and maladministration. The Registry will not look behind the 1987 judgment. In May it rules that the title is 'registered correctly', on the strength of a case about possession and not a single deed to the house.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.4 (87). 21 May 2026 — Cadw's two photographs

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260521-1 · Date: 2026-05-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Cadw releases its two photographs from July 1988, marked 'YYY': 'marginally below the bar', it says. Everything else is gone. The file is 'quite likely' destroyed, it says; by July, 'most likely'. There is no record of anyone destroying it.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/
- Analysis: Cadw — Forensic Critique — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/cadw-forensic-critique-v8-0-0/
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37

### VIII.5 (88). June – July 2026 — The missing root

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260730-1 · Date: 2026-07-30 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

In June the family ask to see the Land Registry's original files, and ask that nothing be destroyed. Six months after their first request, the Registry lists the forty-three documents behind BP's first registration. The 1969 conveyance, the root of BP's title, is not among them.

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.6 (89). 25 August 2026 — "Not held"

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260825-1 · Date: 2026-08-25 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Official correspondence

Museum Wales refuses the family's request: the information is 'not held'. In the same letter it says it has found records of other discoveries at Great House Farm, and withholds them as 'not in scope'.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.7 (90). 8 September 2026 — A lead to 1877

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260908-1 · Date: 2026-09-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Glamorgan Archives hold no deed for the 1877 sale. But they point to the Bute trustees' book of payments for that year, now in Cardiff. If Daniel Thomas paid for the house, it will be written there.

- Official correspondence: The 1877 Agreement — Glamorgan Archives reply — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#glamorgan-2026-4097b

### VIII.8 (91). 17 – 21 September 2026 — Complaints

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260917-1 · Date: 2026-09-17 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

In September the family lodge a formal complaint against Cadw, whose own address blocks it. They write to their MP, Stephen Doughty, asking for the Parliamentary Ombudsman. They ask Heneb, the successor to GGAT, for its files. A Land Registry agent tells them the title was 'closed in 2005', which the Registry's own history contradicts.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/
- Wiki page: The Restoration Campaign — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/restoration-campaign/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — 2026 complaint — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#hmlr-2026

### VIII.9 (92). 23 September 2026 — The Lords papers

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260923-1 · Date: 2026-09-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The National Archives finds the House of Lords papers in BP Properties v Buckler, added to its catalogue only in May 2026. For thirty-eight years, searches had found nothing.

- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.10 (93). 25 – 27 September 2026 — An offer on the woodland

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260925-1 · Date: 2026-09-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Forest of Cardiff, which holds the woodland, offers the family a route to owning it, on its own terms. They turn it down.

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.11 (94). 27 – 29 September 2026 — Keep everything

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260927-1 · Date: 2026-09-27 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Official correspondence

The family take the Land Registry to its Independent Complaints Reviewer, and complain to Heneb about GGAT's part from 1982 to 1995. A preservation notice goes to eleven public bodies: keep everything.

- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Official correspondence: Records Access Chronology — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/

### VIII.12 (95). 29 September – 5 October 2026 — On record all along

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20260929-1 · Date: 2026-09-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

The Royal Commission opens its archive: the 1974 newspaper report, and an old note of the soldier in armour under the dining-room floor. Museum Wales, after two refusals, releases its file on the bones found by the church in 1858. The story was on record all along.

- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
- Official correspondence: Museum Wales reply (GHF-E106-R33) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/ghf-e106-r33-amgueddfa-cymru-reply-further-collections-search-following-8-september-2026-foi/

### VIII.13 (96). September – October 2026 — The question

Act VIII: The Silence · Scene id: ghf-20261006-1 · Date: 2026-10-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Analysis

The family put everything they have found in public: every document and every cutting, from the geese of 1891 to the bus of 1989. And they ask the question no court, no registry and no minister has answered. By what document did the house ever become BP's? No such document has ever been produced.

- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/
- Wiki page: Great House Farm Wiki — Main Page — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/
- Wiki page: Evidence Library — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/
- Wiki page: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/
- Wiki page: Press Articles Index — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### E.1 (97). Today — Who holds it now

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-1 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Analysis

Today twenty houses stand on Great House Farm. BP has sold up and gone. The Land Registry says the title is 'registered correctly'. A thousand of Llandough's dead lie in the stores of the National Museum. The woodland belongs to a charity. The house is gone, and so is the heritage file that might have saved it. BP built the title. The courts upheld it, the Registry recorded it, Cadw declined to protect the house, and the state now holds its dead. Not one of them has said how it happened.

- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/
- Wiki page: Missing Records Register — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/missing-records-register/

### E.2 (98). Today — Not in the history

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990101-2 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Public record

The village's own history page tells of the Roman villa, the lost monastery, and the hundreds of burials dug up in 1994. It does not mention the Great House, the family who lived in it for three hundred years, or the morning it was bulldozed. There has been no public inquiry. No apology. No reparation.

- Public record: Llandough Community Council — About Llandough — https://www.llandough-cc.co.uk/About_Us_20117.aspx
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/

### E.3 (99). Today — What the family ask for

Epilogue: Today · Scene id: ghf-99990102-1 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Family case

The family ask for what was taken. A ruling that the house was theirs. The woodland and the green back, or reparation where that cannot be done. Reparation for the houses built on their land. The estate's artefacts returned. A true record of the Great House in the nation's heritage. And a public inquiry into how all of it was allowed to happen. Every body involved is being given the chance to put it right, before the family go back to court.

- Wiki page: Family Reparations & Remedy Roadmap — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/family-reparations-remedy-roadmap/
- Wiki page: Where Things Stand — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/where-things-stand/
